name: Harrow & The Bone Meridian
description:
Harrow & The Bone Meridian are a seven-piece ensemble formed in 2196 around the singular vision of bandleader and multi-instrumentalist Taraa Mehta-Johanssen, who spent her early career playing Circuit dance halls before a Spire patron funded her a studio and a band. The group — including Cian Osei-Ferreira on modular synth, Daria Volkov-Nduka on erhu-electric, Bolade Svensson on tabla-drum augmentation kit, Yuki Marchetti-Okonkwo on bass, and twin vocalists Ro and Sal Figueiredo-Acharya — play what critics have called 'vertical music': compositions that change character entirely depending on which tier you hear them from.

Physical pressings sold in the Circuit emphasize the rhythm section and the vocalists' raw harmonics. Neural-feed versions sold to Tier 4 subscribers contain additional chrome-frequency layers that restructure the entire emotional architecture of each track. Neither version is dishonest — Mehta-Johanssen insists both are complete works that simply address different ears. Their 2209 album 'Weight Distribution' went cross-tier platinum, a rare commercial and critical phenomenon, and they have played the Spire's Aurelius Hall and the Circuit's Furnace Stage in the same week.
creator: Taraa Mehta-Johanssen
genre: vertical composition, cross-tier fusion, erhu-electric, tabla-augment
audience: Broad cross-tier listenership; Circuit workers, Tier 3 music enthusiasts, Tier 4 cultural consumers, Spire avant-garde patrons
cultural_impact: Harrow & The Bone Meridian are the most commercially successful cross-tier act in GLMZ's recent history, and their success has generated both admiration and deep suspicion. Circuit purists accuse Mehta-Johanssen of selling the working-class sound to Spire audiences; Spire critics dismiss the Circuit versions as 'diluted.' The band's existence — and the ongoing argument about it — has become a lens through which GLMZ debates cultural authenticity, class appropriation, and whether art can genuinely belong to everyone. Their concerts regularly draw crowds that span all tiers, which is itself a logistical and security anomaly.
known_fans: music scholars studying class and sound
story_hooks: A Circuit journalist has obtained evidence that the neural-feed version of 'Weight Distribution' contains subliminal behavioral conditioning — and Mehta-Johanssen may not have known.

The twin vocalists Ro and Sal have separately approached different parties claiming the other is a corporate plant — and someone needs to find out which story is true before the band's anniversary concert.

A Shelf activist group plans to disrupt Harrow's upcoming Aurelius Hall performance as a protest against what they call 'the gentrification of Circuit sound,' and the band's own roadies are sympathetic.
